label: alg:lp-sdp-dual-emission
title: LP/SDP dual-emission contract (first-class infra)
html:
Algorithm (LP/SDP dual-emission contract). Every LP / SDP / operator-selection compute must emit both primal and dual variables in its witness JSON. This sidecar documents the canonical contract.

Required witness fields

Field Meaning
y0_star shadow price of the net constraint
y_star shadow prices of Frobenius positivity constraints (≥ 0)
active_set (or active_constraints / active_channels) indices i with y_star[i] > 0
primal_obj \sum_i t_i x_i^*
dual_obj n_{\mathrm{target}} \cdot y_0^* (= primal_obj by strong duality)
duality_gap \vert \text{primal\_obj} - \text{dual\_obj}\vert

Canonical entry point

The shared solver helpers live at tools/pyhecke/python/pyhecke/lp_dual_solver.py and expose solve_operator_selection_lp(t, G, n_target) and solve_psd_operator_selection_sdp(t, G, n_target). Both return a result whose .to_dict() contains every required field. The per-witness driver script is confinement-operator-selection.py.

Validation

The contract is checked mechanically by computations/lp_dual_witness_validator.py. The validator scans every *.witness.json whose name or description / computation field signals an LP / SDP / operator-selection compute and verifies the dual fields are present.

Why this is mandatory

The dual variables are the binding-energy shadow prices. Active demand channels (y_star[i] > 0) name the receptive sub-braids, identifying the Wedderburn blocks saturated by the bound state. Solving only the primal drops this structural information, a historical flaw (58 of 58 LP/SDP witnesses lacked the dual when this rule was introduced).

Correctness conditions

prop:operator-selection-lp § dual program establishes strong duality (primal_obj = dual_obj to solver tolerance) and the interpretation of y^* as the binding-energy shadow prices.

Python API entry point

from pyhecke.lp_dual_solver import (
    solve_operator_selection_lp,
    solve_psd_operator_selection_sdp,
)

result = solve_operator_selection_lp(t, G, n_target)
witness = result.to_dict()   # primal + dual + active_set + gap

Notes

Not every LP/SDP witness yet carries its dual. The number outstanding changes as the computations are extended, so no figure for it is quoted here.
